findings.description: The EC2 instance's user_data script embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key, which are stored in instance metadata and in Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials
SSH (port 22) is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing anyone on the internet to attempt authentication against the instance
The S3 bucket that receives VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving network traffic metadata unprotected at rest
The instance's attached volume aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk is created without encryption and the instance does not enable an encrypted root device, leaving all disk data unencrypted at rest
The EBS snapshot of the portal disk is unencrypted, exposing the volume's data in any snapshot copy or restore

findings.issue_category: public bucket ACL / no public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and force_destroy = true, so it is not protected against accidental public exposure or deletion
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances in this subnet, unnecessarily exposing hosts to the internet
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances in this subnet, unnecessarily exposing hosts to the internet
A 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway makes the associated route tables public, and those route tables are associated with both subnets
